title: Validate Binary Search Tree
statement: Return `True` if a binary tree is a valid **binary search tree**: for every node, all values in its left subtree are smaller and all values in its right subtree are larger.

example.why: 6 sits in the left subtree of 5 but is larger than 5 — even though it is correctly to the right of 3.

idea: Checking each node only against its own children is **not enough**: a node deep in the left subtree must still be smaller than the root far above it.
Key fact: reading a BST *in order* (left subtree, then the node, then right subtree) produces the values in strictly increasing order.
So do an in-order walk and remember the previous value. The moment a value is not larger than the one before it, the tree is not a BST.

complexity.timeWhy: Each node is read at most once.
complexity.spaceWhy: The recursion stack is as deep as the tree's height h.

steps.text: Our example: **`root = [5,3,8,1,6]`**. Each step runs one highlighted line of the code.
